The Last Call is a song cycle based on several poems by the late Paul Pines. This piece was performed at the Charles R. Wood Theater by 8 singers and 5 live musicians along with tracks Catherine prerecorded on ProTools. An art exhibit of members of North Country Art accompanied this performance with art inspired by the poems Catherine chose for the song cycle.

musicals.title: Holding It All
musicals.desc:
Holding it All is a song cycle based on several poems by the poet Bernice Mennis. Catherine and Anthime Miller each set five poems individually and another two together. North Country Arts hosted the above live recorded performance March 20th 2021 at the Strand Theater.

The recording showcases 4 singers (SATB) and 4 musicians (piano, cello, violin, and woodwinds):

Singers: Kerr Gooden, Barbara Zanoni, John Alecci, Mark Collier.

Instrumentalists: Adam York, Tania Halko Susi, Anthime Miller, and Catherine Reid.

An art exhibit of artwork inspired by the poems will accompany this performance. There will be a CD recording that will be available in the Spring. This project is being funded by LARAC through North Country Arts.

musicals.title: The Yellow Wallpaper
musicals.desc:
The Yellow Wallpaper is a 90-minute opera adapted from the book by Charlotte Perkins Gilman composed by Catherine with libretto Judith C. Lane. It is scored for cello, piano, flute and synthesizer and has a cast of 6 women and one man. It tells the tale of a young writer and mother who is forced to undergo the "rest cure," which was the medical advice given at the turn of the century to women who were exhibiting symptoms of "nervous depression," or were otherwise acting in manners that were not acceptable to society. The "cure" involved many months of complete bed rest, with no reading, no writing, no visitors and no excitement. The main character in The Yellow Wallpaper (who remains nameless throughout the opera) attempts to abide by her doctor/husband's advice and to undergo the rest cure, but it has tragic consequences.

The Yellow Wallpaper received a full production at Peabody Conservatory of Music and was a finalist at the Opera Vista International Opera Competition. Catherine and Judith began writing at YADDO and Virginia Center for the Arts writers colonies and developed the opera through staged readings at the Actor’s Playhouse and American Opera Projects. The opera was a Moore Opera Competition and Eugene O’Neill Musical Theater Conference finalist.

musicals.title: Nearby Faraway
musicals.desc:
Nearby Faraway is a two-act, full-length musical about the lives and art of Georgia O’Keeffe and her husband Alfred Stieglitz composed for 3 musicians and 4 actors with music by Catherine and libretto by Neal Herr. Its production history includes full-length equity readings co-produced by the York Theater with Beth Dunnington, the Musical Theater Project, and featuring J. K. Simmons and Diane Fratantoni at American Opera Projects, as well as selections and slideshow at the Hyde Collection and the Sagamore Hotel and an NPR feature broadcast on Cabaret Central.

These were performed at the Duplex in NYC, and in Saratoga: Spa Little Theater, The Arts Council, The Adelphi Hotel, City Hall, Congress Casino, and Lillian’s.

director.title: The Resistible Rise of Arturo Ui
director.desc:
This show, written by Berthold Brecht, ran for several weeks at the Classic Stage Company (CSC) in NYC. It was directed by Carey Perloff, music directed by Catherine and starred John Turturro, David Patrick Kelly, and Zach Grenier, with music by David Lang. The Resistible Rise chronicles the rise of Arturo Ui, a fictional 1930s Chicago mobster, and is a satirical allegory of the rise of Adolf Hitler and the Nazi Party in Germany prior to World War II.

Read the review of this production in the New York Times.
